findings.title: Inline sequencer quick-edit popovers commit from a stale node snapshot, so a stepper only ever moves by one
findings.detail: Live repro on the desktop build: tapped the Take Exposures count chip (value 4) to open the 'Exposure count' popover, then clicked '+' EIGHT times. The node chip and the thumbnail strip went 4 -> 5 and stopped ('0 / 5 frames'), while the popover kept rendering '4' (shots s50/s51). A ninth '+' still produced 5; two '-' clicks produced 3, i.e. every click re-applies snapshot+-1. Root cause: showInlineNodeEditor passes the node captured at tap time into _InlineEditorBody, which never re-reads the live tree, so each editor commits snapshot.copyWith(...). Affects every inline editor in the file (count, duration, gain, delay, loop iterations, dither pixels, cooling temp, tolerance). Fixed by resolving the node from currentSequenceProvider.nodes[id] on each build. The pre-existing test tapped '+' exactly once, which is why it never caught this; the new test taps three times and expects 8 (fails with 6 when the fix is reverted - verified).
findings.fixSummary: _InlineEditorBody now watches currentSequenceProvider and resolves the live node by id (falling back to the snapshot if it was deleted). Regression test 'the count stepper keeps incrementing on repeated + taps' added to packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/widgets/node_summary_inline_edit_test.dart.

findings.title: Session Report renders a 'Journal' heading with no content and no empty state
findings.detail: In the post-run Session Report the sibling sections all state their empty case ('No guide data recorded for this session.', 'No accepted light frames recorded.'), but 'Journal' renders as a bare heading with nothing under it. Confirmed in the live accessibility tree: 'panel: Journal' is followed immediately by 'panel: Notes' with no child node in between.

findings.title: A run can stall 30 minutes per frame waiting for a meridian flip that is hours overdue and will never fire, and the UI says only 'Running'
findings.detail: Live repro, run #2 (12 x 5s LIGHT on a target at RA 12.5h Dec +70, site 40N 42E). Frame 1 captured and saved normally; the run then froze at '1/12  8%' for the rest of the session. App log at 21:24:12.219964Z: 'Waiting for the meridian flip before the next 5s exposure: the flip fires in ~0s (hour angle +8.93h, threshold 5 min past meridian) and would interrupt the frame'. No 'Capturing frame 2/12' line ever followed. fire_in_secs = (threshold_min - ha*60)*60 goes hugely NEGATIVE when the target is far past the meridian, the gate reads that as 'fires in ~0s' and holds; the only escape is MERIDIAN_GATE_MAX_WAIT = 30 minutes (instructions.rs:1904), which is re-armed before EVERY frame - a 12-frame block would spend ~6 hours idle. The guard above it only rejects the east-of-meridian case (ha <= 0.0); there is no upper bound on how overdue the flip may be. Meanwhile the sequencer header showed 'Running', '1/12  8%', an ETA that had already elapsed, and the sub-line 'Trigger Altitude Limit fired: NextTarget' - nothing anywhere says the run is waiting on a flip, and meridian_flip_progress_dialog never appeared.

findings.title: The Altitude Limit trigger fires every 60s requesting 'next target' when there is no next target, and the run neither advances nor ends
findings.detail: Same live run. The single target sat at 24.8 deg, below the 30 deg Min Altitude default, so the log shows 'Trigger fired: Altitude Limit (altitude_limit) - action: NextTarget' / 'Trigger requested advance to next target' repeating once a minute (21:24:05, 21:25:05, 21:26:05 ...). There is only one target, so nothing advances; the run stays 'Running' forever and the header's only explanation is the sub-line 'Trigger Altitude Limit fired: NextTarget'. A NextTarget action with no next target should end the target (and the run) with a stated reason, not re-fire indefinitely. NOTE: this run was ALSO blocked by the meridian-flip gate above, so the repeat-fire is confirmed but the 'would it otherwise have ended the run' half is not isolated.

findings.detail: Live: run #2 was stopped by hand; the Session Report for it reads 'New Sequence - paused-stopped', Errors 'Sequence cancelled'. The note the app pre-composed for that same run (shot s64) reads '**New Sequence** completed in 4m 44s.' The note is what the user keeps, so it is the copy most likely to be believed later.

findings.title: Enabling the 'Live Frame' dashboard widget blanks the entire primary column - it lays out at infinite height and the engine drops the layer
findings.detail: Live repro: Dashboard > Edit Dashboard > Widgets > tick 'Live Frame' > Done. Now Imaging, Frames and Live Frame are all still ticked in the picker, but the primary column renders NOTHING (shot s90; in edit mode the tiles show as empty placeholders, shot s89). The app log starts emitting 'TransformLayer is constructed with an invalid matrix' at that exact moment (app.log:690 onward, 33 times, none earlier in the session). Cause: dashboard tiles are laid out in a vertical scroll view, so this widget builds with constraints.maxHeight == infinity. RenderFlex with crossAxisAlignment.stretch passes constraints.maxHeight through as a TIGHT height, and _FramePane is a Stack whose children are all Positioned.fill, so the infinity reaches InteractiveViewer's transform and the engine discards the layer subtree - taking its siblings' column with it.
findings.fixSummary: RunDashboardLiveFrame now bounds its own height inside the LayoutBuilder (uses maxHeight when bounded, otherwise a 4:3 box clamped to 180-420px), so no descendant can be laid out at infinite height. Regression test live_frame_panel_unbounded_height_test.dart pumps the widget inside an unbounded-height Column and fails on the infinite-size layout error when the bound is removed.

findings.title: Pre-Flight says the sequence 'has changed since last successful run' while diffing against a run that failed
findings.detail: Live: run #3 completed successfully at 17:33 with 12 accepted frames using exactly 5.0s x12 at RA 22.5000 / Dec 50.0000, and nothing in the sequence was edited afterwards. Pressing Start at 17:57 still raised 'Sequence has changed since last successful run - 2 changes ... 2 modified node(s)', and 'View changes' listed duration 3.0s -> 5.0s, frame count 4 -> 12, RA 12.5 -> 22.5, Dec 70 -> 50 (shot sA8). Those are the values of run #1, which FAILED after one second with zero frames. The comparison base is the last run with a stored snapshot, not the last successful one, and the copy asserts otherwise. Corroborating: the History tab's own 'Diff vs previous run' on the completed run said 'No earlier completed run of this sequence has a saved snapshot to diff against' (shot s95), so no snapshot was taken for the successful run at all.

findings.title: Smart Night's 'Next' looks enabled on the Equipment step but does nothing when the profile has no camera, with no explanation
findings.detail: Live: opened Smart Night with an active profile that has no devices ASSIGNED (the simulators were connected session-only, which the Equipment page itself warns about). Step 1 Window advanced fine. Step 2 Equipment renders 'Camera <no camera>', 'OTA <no telescope> (0mm @ f/0.0)', 'Mount <no mount>'. The Next button is painted in the same enabled blue as on step 1 and the accessibility tree reports it as a plain 'button: Next' with no DISABLED state, but four separate clicks left the stepper on '2. Equipment' (shot sB1) and produced no toast, banner or inline error. The wizard is a dead end that will not say why.
